subtitle: Explore centroid, density, hierarchical, mixture and graph methods. Use embeddings to define a useful geometry, validate stability and let LLMs describe groups without inventing their meaning.
title: Clustering with algorithms, embeddings and LLM-assisted discovery
goal: Discover and validate useful groups without mistaking clusters for ground-truth classes
intro: Explore centroid, density, hierarchical, mixture and graph methods. Use embeddings to define a useful geometry, validate stability and let LLMs describe groups without inventing their meaning.
terms: A group induced by a representation, distance and algorithm.
A mean vector used as a prototype in some clustering methods.
A rule connecting sufficiently dense neighborhoods.
An actual example selected as a representative of a group.
flow: Choose features and distance for the grouping question.
Fit an algorithm whose assumptions match the shape and scale.
Check representatives, noise, stability and usefulness.
Version the grouping and define new-item assignment or refit behavior.
case: Discover recurring themes in synthetic support messages without supplying their category labels to the clustering algorithm.
Inspect actual representative messages, compare groups with a held-out audit label only after fitting, and preserve outliers.
The algorithm produces visually separated groups that follow writing style rather than the product issue.
